Plot Method for RiskMap_cross_validation Objects

Source: R/auxiliary.R
plot.RiskMap_cross_validation.Rd

Plots whatever predictive-performance output is available in a RiskMap_cross_validation object returned by assess_prediction: a spatial map for each per-location metric ("CRPS", "SCRPS", "PIT_area") that was requested via metrics in that call, and/or a calibration curve ("PIT") - the Aggregated normalised Probability Integral Transform (AnPIT) curve for discrete families, or the empirical PIT curve for Gaussian models - when that was requested. Plot titles and legends use AnPIT or PIT according to each model's family. By default every available plot is produced, one per requested model, so you don't need to know in advance which metrics were computed. Each metric gets its own plot (or, with more than one model, its own small grid of one panel per model) rather than everything being squeezed into one combined grid.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap_cross_validation'
plot(
  x,
  metric = NULL,
  model = NULL,
  ...,
  pit_mode = "average",
  pit_test_set = NULL,
  combine_pit = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

A RiskMap_cross_validation object.

metric

Character vector restricting which plot(s) to produce; one or more of "CRPS", "SCRPS", "PIT_area" (a spatial map of that score) and "PIT" (the calibration curve). Defaults to every metric available in x.

model

Character vector of model names to include. Defaults to every model in x$model.

...

Additional ggplot2 components (e.g. scale_color_gradient()), layered onto every spatial-map plot. Must be passed by position only after model, since the remaining arguments must be named.

pit_mode

For the calibration curve only: one of "average" (average curve across test sets, the default), "single" (one specific test set) or "all" (every test set separately).

pit_test_set

Integer; required when pit_mode = "single".

combine_pit

Logical; when pit_mode = "average", draw the calibration curves for every model in a single panel (TRUE) rather than one panel per model (FALSE, default).

Value

When exactly one metric is produced: a single ggplot2 object (one model) or a grid object from gridExtra (more than one model). When more than one metric is produced, each metric's plot/grid is drawn in turn as a side effect (so each one renders as its own figure), and a named list of them - one per metric - is returned invisibly for later reuse.
